title: Why They Marched: Untold Stories of the Women Who Fought for the Right to Vote
author: Susan Ware
target_audience: Students and educators of American history
Activists and advocates for social justice and equality
General audiences seeking stories about the women’s suffrage movement
core_themes: Diversity within the women’s suffrage movement
Personal stories behind the fight for women’s voting rights
Intersectionality: race, class, and regional differences among suffragists
Recovering overlooked or forgotten historical figures
primary_purpose: To illuminate the lesser-known personal stories of a wide range of women involved in the American suffrage movement, demonstrating the complexity, diversity, and impact of their efforts on the road to winning the right to vote.

structure_format.organization: Divided into 19 short chapters, each focusing on a different woman or group, presenting their backgrounds and contributions
features: Contextualization within larger social and political movements

key_concepts_lessons: The fight for women’s suffrage was not monolithic; it was led by women of varied backgrounds, races, and motivations.
Personal stories and individual activism played critical roles in advancing the women’s right to vote.
Recognizing marginalized and overlooked activists expands our understanding of social change.
Historical movements are strengthened by grassroots involvement and a range of perspectives.
Remembering the complexity of the past helps inform present-day struggles for equality.
notable_features: Focus on lesser-known suffragists, including women of color and working-class activists
Accompanied by rare photographs and archival materials
Challenges oversimplified or traditional narratives of the suffrage movement
cultural_historical_context: Released during the centennial of the 19th Amendment (1920–2020), the book contributes to a broader reexamination of women's roles in US history and highlights the previously marginalized voices visible through modern intersectional analysis.
reception_impact: Praised for fresh perspectives and readability in histories of the women’s suffrage movement
Acclaimed for inclusivity and acknowledgment of diverse suffrage activists
Valued by educators, historians, and general readers
Highlights persistent gaps in the mainstream narrative of US suffrage history
comparable_titles: Vanguard: How Black Women Broke Barriers, Won the Vote, and Insisted on Equality for All by Martha S. Jones
Women's Suffrage: The Complete Guide by Elizabeth Frost-Knappman and Kathryn Cullen-DuPont
The Woman’s Hour: The Great Fight to Win the Vote by Elaine Weiss
